messages:
anya: Quick thread 1: We need to reconcile two upgrade patterns for air-gapped sites: full immutable bundle apply vs staged blob streaming with local verification. Want to pick a default UX.

zara: TLDR: full-bundle is simpler for operators (import, verify, activate) but heavy on storage and transport. Staged streaming lets smaller deltas but adds complexity around partial-verify and resumable apply.

samir: another constraint: some customers want per-file signatures (model sharded across blobs) while others accept a single manifest-level signature that covers a merkle root. Which do we endorse?

ben: pragmatic suggestion: manifest-level signature + optional per-blob checksums. Rationale: keep on-disk layout simple and let verifier do fast merkle checks when present. Per-blob signatures only for high-compliance installs.

clara: operator flow idea: 
1) `rwdctl import --bundle bundle.tar.gz` (verifies manifest sig, extracts index)
2) `rwdctl preflight --index local.index` (shows missing blobs, signer info, and expected space)
3) `rwdctl fetch --resume` (for staged streaming agents) or `rwdctl activate --pin sha256:...` (for full-bundle)
We should make `preflight` non-mutating and idempotent.

zara: on resumable fetch: agents must track per-blob state with a compact index (blob_id -> status: missing|verifying|ready). keep index schema tiny (json) so auditors can read.

samir: security note: if we accept manifest-signed merkle roots, an attacker with a compromised network can swap blobs unless we include per-blob checksums in the index and validate them locally. So manifest signature alone is insufficient unless index contains blob digests.

anya: Agree. Manifest must include blob list with digest. Example snippet: ```json
{"manifest_version":"1","root_merkle":"sha256:abc...","blobs":[{"id":"b1","digest":"sha256:...","size":12345},{"id":"b2","digest":"sha256:...","size":98765}]}
```

ben: operationally we should also support an "import-only" mode where operator ships bundle by USB and does `rwdctl import --offline` then runs preflight. That will be a common airgap pattern.

clara: about acceptance tokens: preflight can produce a `consent-token` that is recorded in `audit.jsonl` when operator continues. Format: `{ts, actor, action, manifest_digest, consent_token}`. Keeps exportable logs.

zara: key escrow: two options, (1) include forthcoming public keys inside a `key_rotation` block in the manifest, (2) transmit pubkeys via separate escrow package that operator imports beforehand. Which is less surprising?

samir: option (1) is nicer UX but slightly enlarges bundles. option (2) is explicit and auditable but adds steps. Maybe we make both available: manifests MAY include `rotation_hints` and operator MAY import escrow packages. Default: include rotation_hints for one subsequent signer and require preflight warning.

anya: timing is important. For staged streaming we need a resume token format so partial imports can resume across reboots. Proposed token: base64 of `{manifest_digest, blob_id, offset, nonce}` signed by local agent key to prevent tampering. Keep token readable with `rwdctl resume --token <tok>`.

ben: about rollback: many devices are storage constrained. Keep a small ring buffer of activated manifest digests (default 2). If operator wants longer retention they can opt-in to keep blobs longer. Also provide `rwdctl export-activation --to /tmp/backup` to let support request a portable activation snapshot.

clara: tests: add CI simulation for partial blob corruption during streaming + verify that preflight refuses activation and provides remediation steps (re-import, fetch missing blobs, or accept degraded activation with explicit operator consent).

zara: policy for degraded activation: we should never permit activation if any blob listed in manifest is missing or has bad digest. Acceptance for partial activation is too risky. If operator explicitly forces it, record explicit why and make it clear support may be unable to reproduce.

deploy-bot: NOTE: automation detected a failing unit in `agent/resume` when token contains unexpected nonce length, see https://ci.internal/job/agent-resume/345 (flaky).

anya: good, we'll add token fuzz tests. One last item: we need to standardize the on-disk index file name and location: `.rwd/manifest-index.json` and audit at `.rwd/audit.jsonl`. That makes support easier.

samir: +1. I'll prototype the compact index schema and a JSON schema to validate during import.

ben: +1 on refusing partial activation. Also recommend including a `space_estimate` field in manifest so preflight can tell operator if device has enough temp space for streaming + apply.

anya: action items: zara draft manifest schema with rotation_hints + blob entries; samir prototype index + resume token; clara write CLI UX for import/preflight/fetch/activate/rollback; ben add backup/export tool; I'll update RFC with decisions by EOD.

zara: sounds good. I'll aim to include example `manifest.json` and a small `preflight` output sample in the PR.

anya: thanks all. If no objections in 24h I'll merge the RFC updates. :thumbsup:
